Per-game trait ↔ win correlation (vs FoulPlay)

Within each checkpoint's foul-play games: did the bot use the trait more in games it won? One row per game, so n is games rather than checkpoints — this is the powered version of the aggregate chart below. Confound to keep in mind: longer games contain more of everything, and game length is not independent of the result. 63 checkpoints, 93,500 decided seat-games total. Bar = mean r across checkpoints; whisker = min..max. Bold = every checkpoint agrees in sign (consistency across independent checkpoints is the signal, not any single r).

Per-game trait ↔ win correlation (self-play, paired)

The best-controlled view we have. Both seats are the same policy playing the same game, so comparing the winning seat's behavior against the losing seat's holds policy strength and game length fixed by construction — a game-level quantity has no within-game variance and cannot leak in. 498 checkpoints, 1,976,498 decided seat-games total. Bar = mean r across checkpoints; whisker = min..max. Bold = every checkpoint agrees in sign (consistency across independent checkpoints is the signal, not any single r).

Trait ↔ foul-play win-rate correlation

Pearson r across 63 checkpoints. Both the trait and the win rate are measured on the same foul-play games (v3-foulplay@100k 0.13, v3-foulplay@500k 0.36, v3-foulplay@1000k 0.41, v3-foulplay@1500k 0.45, v3-foulplay@2000k 0.45, v3-foulplay@3000k 0.47, v3-foulplay@4000k 0.50, v3-foulplay@5000k 0.51, v3-foulplay@6000k 0.50, v3-foulplay@7000k 0.51, v3-foulplay@8000k 0.56, v3-foulplay@9000k 0.54, v3-foulplay@10000k 0.53, v3-k0-enthalf@500k 0.41, v3-k0-enthalf@1000k 0.42, v3-k0-enthalf@1500k 0.45, v3-k0-enthalf@2000k 0.44, v3-k0-enthalf@3000k 0.48, v3-k0-enthalf@4000k 0.51, v3-k0-enthalf@5000k 0.52, v3-k0-enthalf@6000k 0.52, v3-k0-enthalf@7000k 0.50, v3-k0-enthalf@8000k 0.54, v3-k0-enthalf@9000k 0.52, v3-k0-enthalf@10000k 0.55, v3-k1-enthalf@500k 0.36, v3-k1-enthalf@1000k 0.41, v3-k1-enthalf@1500k 0.45, v3-k1-enthalf@2000k 0.45, v3-k1-enthalf@3000k 0.47, v3-k1-enthalf@4000k 0.49, v3-k1-enthalf@5000k 0.50, v3-k1-enthalf@6000k 0.48, v3-k1-enthalf@7000k 0.53, v3-k1-enthalf@8000k 0.57, v3-k1-enthalf@9000k 0.56, v3-k1-enthalf@10000k 0.52, v4-enthalf@500k 0.39, v4-enthalf@1000k 0.44, v4-enthalf@2000k 0.49, v4-enthalf@3000k 0.52, v4-enthalf@4000k 0.54, v4-enthalf@5000k 0.54, v4-enthalf@6000k 0.57, v4-enthalf@7000k 0.56, v4-enthalf@8000k 0.56, v4-enthalf@9000k 0.55, v4-enthalf@10000k 0.58, v4-enthalf@11000k 0.55, v4-enthalf@12000k 0.56, v4-enthalf@13000k 0.53, v4-entfull@500k 0.41, v4-entfull@1000k 0.45, v4-entfull@2000k 0.50, v4-entfull@3000k 0.52, v4-entfull@4000k 0.54, v4-entfull@5000k 0.52, v4-entfull@6000k 0.53, v4-entfull@7000k 0.58, v4-entfull@8000k 0.57, v4-entfull@9000k 0.55, v4-entfull@10000k 0.55, v4-entfull@11000k 0.55). Green = trait tracks a higher foul-play win rate, red = lower.

One point per checkpoint, not per game: each checkpoint's 1000 foul-play games collapse into a single (trait, win-rate) pair, so n is the number of checkpoints — game volume buys precision within a point, not more points. It is also an aggregate correlation confounded by overall checkpoint strength (better models do more of everything effective and win more), so read it as association, not cause.

n=63 checkpoints spanning a 0.449 win-rate range.
